English

[edit]
English Wikipedia has an article on:
judo
Wikipedia

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • jūdō

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Japanese 柔(じゅう)道(どう) (jūdō, literally “the soft way”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (UK) enPR: jo͞o'dō, IPA(key): /ˈd͡ʒuːdəʊ/
  • Audio (Southern England):(file)
  • (US) enPR: jo͞o'dō, IPA(key): /ˈd͡ʒudoʊ/
  • Rhymes: -uːdəʊ

Noun

[edit]

judo (uncountable)

  1. A Japanese martial art and sport adapted from jujutsu.
    He started doing judo at the age of eight.

Derived terms

[edit]
  • judoist
  • judolike
  • parajudo, para-judo

Related terms

[edit]
  • judogi
  • judoka

Esperanto

[edit]
Esperanto Wikipedia has an article on:
judoj
Wikipedia eo

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from German Jude, Latin iudaeus.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈjudo/
  • Audio 1:(file)
  • Audio 2:(file)
  • Rhymes: -udo
  • Syllabification: ju‧do

Noun

[edit]

judo (accusative singular judon, plural judoj, accusative plural judojn)

  1. (ethnography, religion) a Jew
    Synonym: hebreo
    Hyponyms: aŝkenazo, judismano, sefardo
    • 1983, Claude Piron, chapter 21, in Gerda malaperis!‎[1], Brazil: Chapecó Fonto, →OCLC, archived from the original on 7 November 2011:
      Katolikoj, protestantoj, ortodoksuloj, judoj, islamanoj, budhanoj kaj aliaj estis membroj de tiu internacia aŭ supernacia societo.
      Catholics, Protestants, Orthodox, Jews, Muslims, Buddhists and others were members of this international or supernational society.
    • 2025 November 12, Thomas Bormann, “La nekredebla viv-historio de Dany Dattel”, in uea.facila‎[2], archived from the original on 11 December 2025:
      Jen la nekredebla viv-historio de Dany Dattel, judo el Germanio.
      Here is the unbelievable life-story of Dany Dattel, a Jew from Germany.

Derived terms

[edit]
  • juda (“Jewish”)
  • judaĉo (derogatory term for a Jew)
  • judaro (“Jews in general, Jewry”)
  • judeco (“Jewishness”)
  • judismano (“practicing Jew, practicier of Judaism”)
  • judismo (“Judaism”)

See also

[edit]
  • ĵudo (“judo”)

Further reading

[edit]
  • “judo”, in Plena Ilustrita Vortaro de Esperanto [Complete Illustrated Dictionary of Esperanto], 2020, →ISBN
  • “judo”, in Reta Vortaro [Online Dictionary] (in Esperanto), 1997-present
  • Grosjean, Émile (1980), “judo”, in Plena Vortaro de Esperanto‎[3], →OL, page 209
